headline: Atlas Arteria falls after sale talks for German motorway asset collapse, while IFM hostile takeover bid continues

Meanwhile, IFM Investors has been conducting a hostile takeover bid and already owns approximately 68% of Atlas Arteria, adding further corporate activity to watch.

headline: Adrian Atkins viewed IFM's offer for Atlas Arteria (LSR) as reasonable given deteriorating conditions, but the core French motorway earnings cliff remains unresolved.
reasoning: Atkins thought the IFM offer for Atlas was reasonable, noting conditions have worsened due to a stronger Australian dollar and new taxes in France. Management compounded problems with an overpriced acquisition and a dilutive equity raising. The fundamental issue is that Atlas loses its French motorway concession in nine years, which contributes around 82% of EBITDA, leaving it subscale. Atlas's plan to outgrow this earnings cliff through acquisitions has not worked well, and Atkins believes overpaying for assets destroys shareholder value. With IFM now holding a majority stake and having been critical of Atlas's acquisitions, future deals will be harder to execute. Atkins concludes that these assets probably make more sense owned by a pension fund.
quote: We also thought the offer for LSR was pretty good, but IFM ended up getting only 67% of shares, so that one's going to remain listed. Clearly, some investors weren't too happy with the offer price, which is a long way below the peak share price from a few years ago. But we actually thought it was reasonable because conditions have actually worsened in recent years, mainly with the stronger Aussie dollar and also new taxes in France. And we think management made things worse with an overpriced acquisition and a dilutive equity raising. So, you know, the core problem for Atlas is that it loses its French motorway in nine years time. And that contributes something like 82% of EBITDA. And after that Atlas will be, we think, subscale with just a couple of small roads and a oversized head office. And there's really no easy way to fix that. Its plan was to outgrow it, to make acquisitions to to offset that earnings cliff. But if you're overpaying for assets then that doesn't really help. It just destroys shareholder value. And we think that that's going to change now with IFM on as the majority shareholder. They've been quite critical of Atlas acquisitions. And so we think there'll be it'll be much harder for them to make acquisitions unless they are clearly adding value. So you know we think that's a good thing. But it doesn't really solve that core issue for Atlas. And that's why we think it probably makes more sense for those assets to be owned by a pension fund.
